subject: Business
title: The Time Value of Money
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Time Value of Money usable.

hook.text: Would you rather have $100 today or $100 a year from now? The answer reveals a fundamental financial law.

buildup.text: The time value of money says a dollar today is worth more than a dollar tomorrow because it can be invested.

discovery.text: Present value calculates what future money is worth today. $1,000 in five years at 5% is worth $783.53 today.

twist.text: This concept explains why lotteries offer lower lump sums than annuity totals. The lump sum today can grow.

climax.text: Every investment decision, mortgage calculation, and retirement plan is built on the time value of money.

punchline.text: A dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow. Every time.

quiz.question: Why is $100 today worth more than $100 in one year?
options: Because $100 today can be invested and grow over the year
Because prices always decrease over time
Because banks charge fees on future money

details.summary: The time value of money states that a dollar today is worth more than a dollar in the future because today's dollar can be invested to earn returns. This concept underpins all of finance, from loan pricing and investment valuation to retirement planning calculations.
details.whyItMatters: Every major financial decision involves comparing money at different points in time. Understanding present and future value calculations is essential for evaluating loans, comparing investment options, and planning for retirement.
takeaways: A dollar today is worth more than a dollar tomorrow due to earning potential
Present value discounts future money back to today's equivalent worth
Future value projects current money forward with expected returns

faq.question: How do you calculate the future value of money?
faq.answer: Multiply the present amount by one plus the interest rate raised to the power of the number of periods. One thousand dollars at 7 percent for 10 years equals 1,000 times 1.07 to the 10th power, approximately 1,967 dollars. This reveals how investments grow over time.

faq.question: What is the practical use of present value calculations?
faq.answer: Present value helps you compare financial options at different points in time. Is a 10,000 dollar payment today better than 15,000 in five years? Discounting 15,000 at your expected return rate reveals its value in today's dollars for a fair comparison.
